title: KODIWA
shortDescription: Property and tenant management platform for Kenya's real estate market — applications, leases, automated invoicing, M-Pesa and bank collections, and maintenance, across web portals and an Android app.
highlights: Took the KCB and Stanbic bank integrations to production — STK push plus instant payment notifications that reconcile rent automatically
Built a tenant credit ledger so overpayments roll into the next invoice, guarded against duplicate M-Pesa confirmations
Reworked the arrears and delinquency calculations and added bulk SMS and WhatsApp payment reminders

overview: Kodiwa is property and tenant management software built for Kenya's rental market. It runs the whole tenant lifecycle in one system: rental applications, offer letters, leases, rent invoicing, payment collection and reconciliation, maintenance, and landlord payouts.

Rent in Kenya arrives through M-Pesa paybills, STK pushes, bank paybills, and SMS alerts, and most agencies reconcile it by hand across statements, spreadsheets, and WhatsApp. Kodiwa collects through those same channels, matches payments to invoices as they land, follows up arrears by SMS and WhatsApp, and produces landlord statements and payouts.

It serves four audiences through separate web panels — platform admin, agency staff (owner, finance, main office, and caretaker roles), a tenant self-service portal, and a read-only landlord portal — plus an Expo / React Native app with a role-specific home screen for each. I'm a co-founder, and my engineering work centres on the money: payment integrations, billing logic, arrears, and expenses.

title: SAT ERP INTEGRATOR
shortDescription: The integrations between Solutech's sales automation platform and clients' ERPs — SAP Business One, Oracle, Dynamics 365 Business Central, Acumatica, Sage, SYSPRO, Odoo, Tally, and Epicor iScala — syncing master data, sales documents, and tax e-invoices in both directions.
highlights: Built SAP Business One sync for blanket agreements and much of sales-invoice posting, price lists, and customer special prices
Built the Acumatica ERP connector end to end — OAuth, master-data pulls, order posting, and inbound webhooks
Built the Sage 200 Evolution integration, with order-status tracking through a database trigger and outbox
overview: Solutech's Sales Automation Tool (SAT) runs field sales for manufacturers and distributors — reps taking orders, collecting payments, and checking stock on the road. None of that is useful unless it reaches the ERP that actually runs the business, and every client runs a different one.

The integrations grew in two generations. First, ERPs were wired straight into SAT: controllers that post orders, sales invoices, deliveries, and payments into SAP Business One and other ERPs, and pull customers, products, price lists, and stock back into staging tables. Then came an on-premise Laravel integrator that sits next to the ERP, runs scheduled master-data and document syncs, reads over ODBC or the ERP's own API, maps fields through configuration, and writes back through the most native route each ERP offers — COM SDKs, REST, SOAP, or XML.

With the integrator, new clients are onboarded mostly by configuration — ERP type, field mappings, and per-ERP SQL query packs — rather than new code. I worked across both generations for three years: SAP Business One and Acumatica integrations in the platform, and the Sage 200 Evolution integration and diagnostics tooling in the integrator.

title: VOCHI
shortDescription: AI customer-communication platform — AI voice calls, an embeddable chat widget, WhatsApp and Telegram, appointment booking, and CRM sync with HubSpot, Zoho, Salesforce, and Airtable.
highlights: Built a Google Drive → Qdrant knowledge-ingestion pipeline orchestrated by n8n
Built retrieval-augmented chat that answers from a team's documents across the web widget and WhatsApp
Fixed duplicate channel messages, outbound demo calls, and the WhatsApp webhook handshake
overview: Vochi is a multi-tenant SaaS that puts AI assistants on a business's phone lines and chat channels — inbound and outbound voice calls, an embeddable website widget, WhatsApp, and Telegram. Teams configure each assistant's voice, prompt, and knowledge, and can chain several into crews that hand a conversation between specialists.

It's built for small and mid-sized teams that can't answer every call, qualify every lead, or book every meeting. Assistants answer from the team's knowledge base, book into connected calendars, sync leads to the CRM, and escalate hard cases to people as support tickets.

My work focused on knowledge: letting customers connect their own document sources and making assistants answer from them with retrieval-augmented generation, plus reliability fixes across chat, WhatsApp, voice, and lead import. Most of the knowledge work was built and tested on staging feature branches rather than merged into the production app, and Vochi is currently offline.
